                                    PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 2
                                  CHAPTER-I
                         ABOUT THE COLLEGE
       HCDG College is an Arts College basically imparting higher education in Social
Sciences and Humanities. The college, however, has embarked on creating opportunities
for unprivileged students of this remote rural area so that parents of aspiring students do
not have to travel far in their pursuance of higher education.

                                      MISSION
               Our Mission is academic pursuit and professional competency.
       The college seeks to promote learning and scholarship for the
       service of the society and the humanity.
               Here the college fraternity strives hard to create an
       environment for all round development of the students in academic
       and personal level. HCDG College aims at inculcating human values
       and social responsibility for a better future and to empower the
       students to face the challenges of this competitive world.


                                       VISION
               HCDG College strives to become a premier educational
       institution of higher education in this rural area. The institution
       endeavours to imbibe in students the value and importance of
       education and to make the student realize his/her real potential
       and to utilize the same in achieving upward social mobility.

                                  OBJECTIVES
  ¾ The institution endeavours to spread the message of importance of education in
     the present globalized world among the students of this rural area.
  ¾ To make this institution one of the best rural centres of higher education by providing
     the students quality education through the use of modern infrastructure.
  ¾ To imbibe a sense of social consciousness among the students by engaging them in
     various extension activities and community service/work.
  ¾ To shape them as individuals and citizens contributing, according to their capacity, to

                                                                 PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 3
      the well being and progress of the society.
 ¾ To inculcate in them a sense of belonging to the country and thereby spread the
     message of national integration.
 ¾ To develop their personality so that they can find themselves fit to compete with
     others in the struggle for life as confident young men and women.
 ¾ To make them fit and capable to gain accessibility to upward social mobility through
     proper education.
 ¾ To make them understand the importance of education in modern society and spread
     this message among their peers in their respective fields and thereby help in the
     spread of literacy.
 ¾ To make them aware of their democratic rights and responsibilities so that they can
     be shaped as conscious and law abiding citizens of the country.
 ¾ To broaden their outlook in a way to make them capable to think in terms secularism
     and rise above parochial considerations.
 ¾ To develop in them love for fine arts and attract them to explore their inherent
     artistic talent.
 ¾ To make them aware of the environment so that they can be conscious and active to
     the issues of conservation of the environment.


                BRIEF HISTORY OF THE COLLEGE

      Set in the sylvan surrounding of expansive paddy fields, Nitaipukhuri, historically an
important place of Assam, offers a great visual treat of natural beauty. The Dehing River
flows quietly to the south and to the north there is the National Highway-37, connecting it
with all major towns of Assam. Nitaipukhuri is the nerve centre of more than fifty six
smaller villages that dot the landscape around it.
      Ever since 1960 the need of a college was felt by the conscious masses of this area
who wanted to shape the future of the younger generation by providing them an
opportunity to pursue higher education without having to travel far and spend-ing an
unaffordable amount. In 1965 a managing Committee was constituted consisting of a few
educationists of this area like late Tarun Gogoi, Sri Kukheswar Gogoi, first President and
Secretary respectively. Under their able stewardship the college was established and was


                                                                  PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 4
 named after the then Auniatiya Satradhikar, Majuli, Hem Chandra Deva Goswami who
had donated generously to construct the main building of the college. The regular
academic session commenced in July 1965. The Managing Committee and everybody
associated with it worked tirelessly and selflessly to give shape to this nascent institution.
Lt. Mina Dutta became the next Secretary of this Managing Committee and continued the
effort of taking this institution a step forward. It was during his secretaryship the college
continued its mission of catering to the educational needs of the students of this
backward area in-habited by many ethnic groups. The college was brought under Grants-
in-Aid Scheme on 1st July 1977. Finally, in September 1998 the college got registered under
2 (f) and 12 (b) clause of University Grants Commission. In 2003 the college also got the
permanent affiliation of the Assam Higher Secondary Education Council, Guwahati. At
present the college is permanently affiliated to the Dibrugarh University, Dibrugarh,
Assam. In February, 2017 the college has been accredited by NAAC with a B grade.
The college has been adopting itself to face the new challenges in the field of higher
education and continues to strive to excel in the changed educational scenario.

                                          IQAC
      The college has established Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) for the all
round development of the institution. IQAC in this college was formed as per the
guidelines of National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC).


                           RESEARCH COUNCIL
      To monitor research activities, to ensure quality research and to give a pace to
research works in the institution, a Research Council has been formed in the college with
the Principal as its Director, and Dr. Leena Dutta, as Secretary, and two senior teachers
from each department as its members.
                                     ECO CLUB
      The Eco Club of HCDG College has been empowering its members to participate
and take up meaningful environmental activities and projects. Eco Club is under the
supervision of Dr. Diganta Gogoi, and teaching, non-teaching staff, library staff and
students are the members.
            SATTRIYA NRITYA VISHARAD COURSE
     Sattriya nritya Visharad course is introduced in collaboration with Nrityalaya,
Demow. It follows the course prescribed by Sankari Sangeet Vidyapeeth, Dhekial,
Golaghat. Pubali Thengal Gogoi and Rupali Dutta are the teachers. The course is open for
all.

                         DEPARTMENTS

                             ASSAMESE

     The department of Assamese was started in 1965 with the very inception of
the college. Later on MIL and Advance Assamese, and Major in Assamese were
introduced. Dr. Prahlad Kumar Barua, one of the doyens of Assamese literature,
was appointed as a faculty in this department.
     The department provides opportunity to the teachers and students to involve
in academic and extra-curricular activities.
Present Faculty :

            Dr. Niva Das. M.A., Ph.D
            Dr. Pikumoni Chutia, M.A., M.Phil., Ph.D
            Dr. Mridusmita Dutta. M.A., M.Phil, Ph.D.

                             ECONOMICS

       Department of Economics was started with the very inception of the college.
B.A(Honors) in Economics was started in 1978 and received concurrence from the
Dibrugarh University, Dibrugarh in 1979. Honours in Economics started with 8
students, and all are well established now. The department comprises dedicated and
qualified faculties who effort tirelessly for the upliftment of the students. The
department organizes National seminar, extra- curricular activities and makes the
students involve in some extension activities.

Present faculty :
            Mrs. Bornali Saikia Sonowal. M.A. B.Ed. M. Phil (HoD)
            Sri Ronjit Khanikar. M A.
            Mrs. Nilakshi Goswami, M.A.
            Mr. Hemanta Bori (Temporary)




                            EDUCATION

      The department of Education was started in 1965 with the inception of the
college. A number of dedicated teachers have been working in this department.
Students passed out from this department have attained placements in different
parts of India.

    There is a Psychological Laboratory in this department.

Present faculty :
            Mrs Dipali Gogoi. M.A.(HoD)
            Mrs Manashi Gogoi. M.A.
            Dr. Leena Dutta, M.A. Ph.D.
            Dr. Rashmi Rekha Duwarah, M.A. M.Phil. Ph.D


                                                            PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 7
                                   ENGLISH
     The department of English was established in 1965, and Major in English was
introduced in 1993. A number of qualified teachers have been serving in the
department since its inception. The department encourages creative and critical
thinking and writing skill development instead of rote learning, memorization and
cramping. Along with classroom pedagogy screening of films, literary and scholarly
discussions, recitation, competitions are held for better understanding of literature
and developing Soft Skill.
     It has a well stocked library and an e-library for the easy access to the teachers
and students.

Present faculty:
             Mrs Gitali Saikia. M.A. (HoD)
             Mrs. Meghali Boruah. M.A. B.Ed
             Mrs. L.X. Polin Hazarika, M.A.




                                  HISTORY
    Though this department was started from the inception of the college Major in
History was introduced in 1993. This department has a forum for arousing
awareness for preservation of rich cultural heritage and historical monuments in
surrounding areas. The department produces rank holders in BA Final
Examinations held under Dibrugarh University. The department has a library with
600 books.

Present faculty :
             Sri Sivaranjan Sharma. M.A.
             Dr. Tarun Gogoi. M. A. M.Phil., Ph.D (HoD)
             Sri Horen Bhuyan. M.A.

                       POLITICAL SCIENCE
     The department of Political Science is an integral part of the college since its
inception. . The department has a well stocked library. “Raj Chora” is its Wall
Magazine, published annually. The department conducts academic and extra-
curricular activities for the benefit of the students. The Department has ‘Whats
App Group’ for communication and intercommunication, for better circulation of
knowledge.

professional competency of the students. The college provides more computers

                              CHAPTER-II

                     ADMINISTRATIVE REGULATIONS

                                College Rules
   1. The Academic session of the College begins from June.
   2. Admission procedure begins after the declaration of the result of the SEBA,
     AHSEC and University and continues till the last day prescribed by the Council or
     University.
   3. The College offers instruction in the courses of Arts stream only.

                                                              PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 9
                               Admission Procedure
  1. For admission in to H.S. 1st year and Semester- I, the candidate should apply in the
     prescribed application form along with self attested copies of the certificate and
     mark-sheet of the last qualifying examination passed.
      NO XEROX OR ANY OTHER REPRODUCED COPY OF THE
      PRESCRIBED FORM OF APPLICATION WILL BE ACCEPTED.
  2. Documents required at the time of admission:
      (i) Provisional certificate of the qualifying examination last passed.
      (ii) Mark sheet of the last qualifying examination passed.
      (iii) Gap certificate (if required) from the appropriate authority.
      (iv) Two copies of recent passport size photograph (colour or black & white).
      Self attested copies of above documents should be submitted along with the
      application form. However, at the time of interview for admission all these
      documents must be produced in original.
  3. Mid-term admission in transfer cases beyond the normal admission period will be
     accepted only after getting prior permission from the Council/ University as the
     case may be.
                                   Identity card
      After admission each and every student of the college will be issued an      identity
card which is non-transferable. The identity card should be carried all the time by the
students. For issuance of duplicate identity card the students should apply in plain paper
with a signed passport size photograph to the Principal and deposit an amount of fine as
fixed by the authority.
                              Change of Address
    Any subsequent change of address (present/permanent) of the student should be
immediately intimated to the college office in writing.
                              Change of Subjects
      Under exceptional case change of subject is allowed only in H.S. Courses. The
student should apply to the principal within two weeks of the completion of admission
process.
        Change of subject is not allowed in Semester system.
                                   Fee Structure
     Fees will be decided as per Assam Govt. Rule for colleges of rural areas and
Dibrugarh University notification.

 Grading System
1. The absolute grading system shall be applied in evaluating performance of the students.

2. The following scale of grading system shall be applied to indicate the performances of
students in terms of letter grade and grade points as given below:

        Letter Grade with meaning                            Grade Point
      O              Outstanding 10                  (Marks securing above 90%)
      A+              Excellent 9                     (Marks securing 80%-90%)
       A              Very Good 8                    (Marks securing 70% -80%)
      B+               Good 7                        (Marks securing 60% -70%)
      B             Above Average 6                  (Marks securing 50% -60%)
       P                  Pass 5                     (Marks securing 40% -50%)
       F                Fail 0                       (Marks securing below 40%)
      Abs         Absent/ Incomplete                              0



                           WEAVING TRAINING CENTRE

        HCDG College has started “Earn while you learn” programme for aspiring poor
students. In 2017 WEAVING TRAINING COURSE is introduced in the college to provide
opportunity of higher education for the under-privileged students who can earn money
during the period of their learning.
                             BEAUTY THERAPY COURSE

       Self-sustaining Certificate Course in Beauty Therapy will be started from the
forthcoming session for the aspiring students.
                                          SWAYAM
       SWAYAM is a programme initiated by Government of India and designed to achieve
the three cardinal principles of Education Policy viz., access, equity and quality. The objective
of this effort is to take the best teaching learning resources to all, including the most
disadvantaged. Under SWAYAM we are trying to open up new avenues for our aspiring
learners.

                                   CHAPTER-IV
                                  COLLEGE LIBRARY
        The college library contains over 10,000 books; it subscribes 19 journals and
periodicals, 8 Assamese and 4 English daily newspapers at present. It has a reading
room with internet facility. The college is registered under N-List Inflibnet e-Library, an
initiative of Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) under the NME-ICE,
funded by UGC, under UGCINFONET Digital Library Consortium. Nlist Inflibnet
Library extends access to 6000+ e-journals, 31,35,000+ e-books.
        There is also a digital library szection where 3,000 books including theses, journals
and magazines are preserved.
Photocopying Facility
        The library provides photocopying facility to the readers at subsidized rates.
Circulation
       Issue/return/renew of books has been digitalized in the library. Barcode based
circulation is introduced from 2016. The library staff is always ready to provide necessary
information required by the users.
Reader’s Card
      Every admitted student by submitting the money receipt at the library counter can
collect his/her library card. The reader’s card remains valid up to the filling up of forms
for the examination.
Transaction of Books
       A maximum number of two books shall be issued to a student and he/she can
retain the books for a maximum period of two weeks or 15 days.
       The same must be returned on the due date, failing which a fine of Rs. 2/- per book
will be levied for every overdue day.
       At the time of issuing books, the student is advised to check the pages, if there is
any damage or mutilation of pages found, it should be brought to the notice of the librarian
instantly. The librarian reserves the right to recall any book at any time. In case of loss of
any book or part thereof shall have to be replaced by the borrower or double the cost of
the book may be deposited.
Book Bank Facility
       A Book Bank was started in the college library in 2011 for providing text books to
poor and meritorious students (both Higher Secondary and Degree students). At present
it has 1355 books.
                                                                  PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 15
                 THIS YEAR MORE STUDENTS WILL BE
                COVERED UNDER THE BOOK BANK FACILITY.

                                EXEMPTION OF FEES
1. Poor meritorious students (generally) belonging to SC/ST are exempted from payment
of admission fee and tuition fee on production of caste and annual income certificate
from the competent authority.
2. SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/Minority/Economically deprived (BPL card holder)/ Physically
Challenged Degree students of the college will be given a periodic stipend.
3. Girl students are exempted from payment of tuition fee in H.S. Course only.
                               ISSUE OF CERTIFICATE
i) All kinds of certificate shall ordinarily be issued within three days of application.
ii) When an original certificate is lost by an ex-student a duplicate transfer certificate/
college leaving certificates may be issued on application by the candidate after payment of
the requisite fees.
                                       DISCIPLINE
(a) College uniform for the students:
       Boys: Black trousers and white shirt with Badge.
       Girls : White mekhela-chadar with sky-blue border and matching blouse in sky blue/
       white kurta & sky blue paijama with sky blue dupatta with Badge.
(b) College Uniform is must for all the students.
(c) All students are required to attend their classes regularly and punctually. Continuous
absence from the class without prior permission or information is a serious breach of
discipline of the college.
(d) A student should maintain class room decency at any cost and any breach of decorum
inside the class room will be viewed seriously.
e) Students are prohibited from loitering on the verandah or crowding in front of the
office.
f) Students are not allowed to join any political party or indulge in any political activity in
the college campus.
g) Students should put their grievances before the Grievances Redressal Cell in writing or
consult the Prof.-in-charge.
h) Students should not damage the electrical fittings; disfigure walls by spitting break window
panes, desk or benches and other college property. This is a punishable offence. Any

                                                                    PROSPECTUS 2020-2021 16
 student involved in such activities must replace the same as per the decision of the
Grievances Redressal Cell.
i) Use of intoxicants and smoking inside the college campus is strictly prohibited. Erring
students will be severely dealt with.
j) No students can represent any activity in the name of the college without prior permission
of the college authority.
k) Mobile Phones and other such devices can not be used inside the class room.
Violation of any of the clauses mentioned above may be punished by a fine, suspension,
rustication or expulsion as deemed fit by the authority.
Attendance
       A student is required to attend a minimum 85% of the lecture delivered in the
session to be eligible to appear in college/Council/University examinations.
       Condonation of attendance may be granted by the Principal in exceptional cases if
he is satisfied by the reason(s)
Examination
    i)    The H.S/Semester students will have to appear at Unit Examinations to be eligible
          to submit their final Examination Form(s)
     ii) For Semester students there shall be one University conducted (End Semester)
          examination usually in the month of May/November in every six months.
Internal Assessment for Degree Students as per DU rules:
The marks allotted for Internal Assessment (20%) in each course shall be based on the
following:
(a) Sessional Examination I (Written): 25% of the marks allotted for Internal Assessment
(b) Sessional Examination II (Written): 25% of the marks allotted for Internal Assessment.
(c) Seminar / Group Discussion etc.: 25% of the marks allotted for Internal Assessment.
(d) Attendance: 25% of marks allotted or Internal Assessment
                 Range of % of Attendance            Marks to be awarded
                 80 % to less than 85 %                       2
                 85 % to less than 90 %                       3
